sg.name: Declined form without its ending (singular or indefinite)

sub.name: Finite verb form without its relative -n or complementizer -la

pfx.name: Finite verb form without a prefix (ba-, bait-, ez-) or a familiar ending

transforms.name: -n (relative, subjunctive)
transforms.description: Relative or subordinate -(e)n on a finite verb: den (that is), duen (that has), dudan, nagoen, datorren; also the subjunctive (nadin, dezan) and indirect questions.

transforms.name: -(e)la (that)
transforms.description: Complementizer -(e)la on a finite verb: dela (that it is), duela, dudala, naizela, zela (that it was); with -ko, because (delako, delakoan), and -rik, while (delarik).

transforms.name: ba- (if; affirmative)
transforms.description: ba- on a finite verb: the condition of a hypothesis (bada, if it is; balitz, if it were) or an affirmative stress (badakit, I do know).

transforms.name: bait- (because, since)
transforms.description: bait- on a finite verb: because, since (baita, since it is; baitu, bainaiz, baikara, baitzen).

transforms.name: familiar (hika, to a man)
transforms.description: Familiar speech to a male friend: -k on the verb (gaitezkek, noakiok), with z- for d- (zagok, zabiltzak).

transforms.name: -an for -en (familiar or western past)
transforms.description: A past form with -an for -en: familiar speech to a man (nekian, zegoan) and western and older writing (zan, zuan, zegoan for zen, zuen, zegoen).

transforms.name: ez- (not) joined to the verb
transforms.description: ez (not) written with the verb, as in speech: ezta (= ez da, isn't it), ezpada (= ez bada, if not), ezkara (= ez gara).

transforms.name: comparative
transforms.description: Comparative degree: -ago (handiago, bigger; zaharrago, older).

transforms.name: superlative
transforms.description: Superlative degree: -en, usually with the article (handiena, the biggest; onena, the best).

transforms.name: excessive
transforms.description: Excessive degree: -egi (handiegi, too big; zaharregi, too old).

transforms.name: comparative or superlative (irregular)
transforms.description: Irregular degree: hobe (better) and hoberen (best) of on, gehiago, gehien and gehiegi of asko, hobeto (better) of ondo.

transforms.name: future participle
transforms.description: Future (prospective) participle, -ko, or -go after -n (-en after -n and -l in the east: eginen): ikusiko (will see), etorriko, egingo, joango. With an auxiliary it makes the future (ikusiko dut, I will see it).

transforms.name: ablative (animate)
transforms.description: Local case of a person or animal, attached to the genitive: -gandik (gizonarengandik).

transforms.name: allative (animate)
transforms.description: Local case of a person or animal, attached to the genitive: -gana (gizonarengana).

transforms.name: terminative (animate)

transforms.name: destinative (animate)
transforms.description: Local case of a person or animal, attached to the genitive: -ganako (gizonarenganako, towards the man).

transforms.name: adverb (-ki)
transforms.description: Adverb of manner made from an adjective with -ki: ederki (finely, well) from eder.

transforms.name: locative genitive (-ko) of an adverb
transforms.description: Adverbs take -ko with no -e- after a consonant, and -go after -n: gaurko (today's), atzoko, hemengo, oraingo.

transforms.name: distributive (-ka)
transforms.description: Adverb made with -ka from a noun, adjective or numeral: ehunka (by hundreds), bakarka (one by one), taldeka (in groups), oihuka (shouting).

transforms.name: ablative of an adverb
transforms.description: Adverbs take -tik with no -e- after a consonant, and -dik after -n: hortik (from there), gaurtik, hemendik, handik.

transforms.name: allative, terminative or directive of hemen, hor, han
transforms.description: Hona (to here), horra and hara are the allatives of hemen, hor and han; honaino, honantz and the others their terminative and directive.

transforms.name: imperfective participle
transforms.description: Imperfective participle, -t(z)en: ikusten (seeing), egiten, hartzen, etortzen. With an auxiliary it makes the present and the past habitual (ikusten dut, I see it).

transforms.name: verbal noun
transforms.description: Verbal noun, -t(z)e, declined like a noun: ikustea (seeing), egiteko (in order to do), joatera (to go), hartzean (when taking).

transforms.name: radical (short form)
transforms.description: Radical of a verb, the participle without -tu, -du, -i or -ri, used before the subjunctive, potential and imperative auxiliaries: ikus (ikus dezagun, let us see), har ezazu (take it), jar, itzul, konpon, joka.

transforms.name: auxiliary
transforms.description: The verb an auxiliary root belongs to: *edin is izan's (nadin, daiteke), *ezan is *edun's (dezan, dezake, ezazu).

transforms.name: compound verb
transforms.description: The first word of a compound verb cited with izan, written apart from its auxiliary: uste (uste izan, to think), nahi (nahi izan, to want), maite (maite izan, to love).

transforms.name: resultative participle (-ta, -da)
transforms.description: Participle of a state or a completed action, -ta, or -da after -n and -l: ikusita (having seen), nekatuta (tired), eginda (done), hilda (dead).

transforms.name: relative participle (-tako, -dako)
transforms.description: Participle used before a noun, -tako, or -dako after -n and -l, declined like an adjective: ikusitako (seen), egindako (done), esandakoa (what was said).

transforms.name: ablative (animate)
transforms.description: The ablative (animate) of a pronoun, demonstrative or interrogative, whose stem changes: nik (I), honek (this one), horretan (in that), zertan (in what).

transforms.name: allative (animate)
transforms.description: The allative (animate) of a pronoun, demonstrative or interrogative, whose stem changes: nik (I), honek (this one), horretan (in that), zertan (in what).

transforms.name: pronoun, determiner or numeral
transforms.description: A determiner, pronoun or numeral, which dictionaries list without a part of speech, after its case ending was removed: bestea, batean, zenbatek, norbaiti, biak, hiruretan.

transforms.name: familiar past
transforms.description: Past indicative in familiar speech to a friend (hika), which marks the listener; the forms name the persons.

transforms.name: past conditional
transforms.description: Past conditional (would have); the forms name the persons.

transforms.name: past potential
transforms.description: Past potential (could have); the forms name the persons.

transforms.name: past subjunctive
transforms.description: Past subjunctive (so that ... would); the forms name the persons.

transforms.name: hypothetical (with a dative)
transforms.description: Hypothetical stem, the condition of a hypothesis, written after ba- (if) or bait-, with a dative person (nori); the forms name the persons.

transforms.name: hypothetical potential (with a dative)
transforms.description: Hypothetical potential (could, might), with a dative person (nori); the forms name the persons.
